newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to extend Golan Heights peacekeeping.
newsitem.headline: Japan to extend Golan Heights peacekeeping.

text.p: Japanese troops taking part in U.N. peacekeeping operations in the Golan Heights will extend their term of duty for an additional two years beyond next February, defence ministry officials said on Thursday.

Ministry officials said Japanese Defence Minister Fumio Kyuma will propose Japan's extended contribution to the U.N. Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) when he meets with UNDOF commander Major General David Stapleton in Syria on Friday.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto was expected to formalise the decision at a cabinet meeting later this month, the ministry officials said.
Japan's 45-member army logistics unit is part of the 1,000-member UNDOF which also comprises troops from Poland, Austria and Canada.

The unit from the Ground Self-Defence Force, or army, was first sent to the Golan Heights in February 1996 for a two-year term, Japan's first contribution to a peacekeeping operation in the Middle East.
Japan has also sent troops for U.N. peacekeeping operations in Cambodia and Mozambique as well as to Zaire in support of a relief operation for Rwandan refugees.
